messages:
Ivy: Quick sync—post-RFC, we still need a production plan for continuous batching compaction vs per-tenant isolation. Key constraints: KV cache stability, p99 tail, and predictable billing.

Tom: My hot take: keep per-tenant queues by default, enable cross-tenant packing only on dedicated nodes or when pack ROI > X.

Zara: Agreed on default. Also add a runtime opt-in classifier: tenants with median_seq_len > 128 and token_rate > Y are good pack candidates.

Ben: Implementation nit: do micro-compacts with a budget and cooperative yields. If compaction runs on dispatch cores we saw ~150ms p99 spikes in staging.

Ivy: We'll reuse headroom credits so compaction pauses under pressure. Also expose pack_ratio metric and a planner hook to recompute cost models if pack_ratio changes significantly.

Tom: Add per-tenant opt-out for legal/tenant-isolation. And a Console kill-switch + backlog panel for oncall.

Zara: For KV interactions, add pinned_kv_eviction telemetry and throttle compaction if evictions climb.

Ben: I'll prototype the micro-compact loop and yield logic. Tom can add planner hook. Ivy will update the RFC with the three-mode default (noop/local/cross) and ledger integration.

ci-bot: CI queued for branch batch-compaction-proto (PR #4801). Tests will post status here.

Ivy: Great. Target prototype by EOW, then run a small A/B on dedicated nodes next maintenance window. Ping if blockers.
